title: The Energy of a Diatomic/Polyatomic Molecule Can Be Approximated as a Sum of Separate Terms
lead: A molecule can store energy in translation, rotation, vibration and its electrons. Treating these as independent turns the partition function of a gas of molecules into a product of one factor per kind of motion, and gives a recipe for each factor's share of the heat capacity.
exercise_notes: The book sets no exercises for this section; the one here is new and AI-written, with an AI solution. Its Bloom level and concept tags were chosen by AI.

exercises.source_id: The partition function of a molecular idea gas is then:
exercises.prompt: Of the four factors in $\kQsys = (\kqtrans\kqvib\kqrot\kqelec)^N/N!$, which depend on the volume? Use $\langle P\rangle = k\kT(\partial \ln \kQsys/\partial \kV)_{N,\kT}$ to show what this means for the pressure of an ideal gas of molecules.

answer.hint: The rotational, vibrational and electronic levels belong to one molecule and do not change when the box does.
answer.solution: Only $\kqtrans = \kV/\Lambda^3$ depends on $\kV$; the rotational, vibrational and electronic levels are those of one molecule and do not change with the box. So $\ln \kQsys = N\ln \kV + (\text{terms without } \kV)$, and $(\partial \ln \kQsys/\partial \kV)_{N,\kT} = N/\kV$. Then $\langle P\rangle = Nk\kT/\kV$ for every ideal gas, whatever its molecules: rotation, vibration and electronic structure change the energy and the heat capacity of the gas but not its equation of state.

footnotes.html: The energies add, as the sentence says: $E_\text{tot} = E_\text{trans} + E_\text{vib} + E_\text{rot} + E_\text{elec}$. The book prints them as a product.
